title: Can Genoa Help UNH Expand Its Behavioral Health Pharmacy Business? - The Globe and Mail
content: UnitedHealth Group Incorporated UNH is expanding its presence in behavioral healthcare through Genoa Healthcare, an Optum Rx business serving people with mental health conditions and substance use disorders. Its specialized pharmacy model gives UnitedHealth an opportunity to reach underserved populations, strengthen relationships with behavioral health providers and diversify its pharmacy services. Genoa operates more than 750 pharmacies across 48 states and Washington, D.C., partnering with more than 500 community mental health providers. By locating pharmacies within behavioral health facilities, Genoa makes medications more accessible and enables closer coordination between pharmacists and clinicians. Personalized medication management and refill assistance can also help patients maintain complex, long-term treatments. The expansion comes as Optum Rx faces a decline in prescription volumes. Its adjusted prescriptions fell to 393 million in the third quarter of 2026 from 414 million a year earlier, primarily due to membership contraction at UnitedHealthcare and other customers. Expanding Genoa's network could add another source of prescription volume and create opportunities to deepen provider partnerships. However, Genoa's standalone financial contribution is not disclosed, making it difficult to assess its current impact on Optum Rx's results. Genoa's longer-term contribution will depend on its ability to attract new patients, expand provider partnerships and increase prescription activity while managing operating costs. A larger network could improve the reach of its specialized pharmacy services and support recurring prescription volumes. With growing demand for behavioral healthcare and stronger integration between pharmacy and clinical services, Genoa could become a valuable growth driver for Optum Rx over time. UnitedHealth faces competition from peers Elevance Health, Inc.ELV and CVS Health Corporation CVS, which are also expanding integrated healthcare services, including pharmacy access, medication management and behavioral care. Elevance Health is strengthening coordinated care through Carelon, which combines behavioral health and pharmacy services. ELV's Community Pharmacy Total Care program connects members with independent pharmacies for personalized medication management, custom packaging and adherence support. CVS Health is expanding behavioral healthcare access through Aetna and MinuteClinic, complementing its extensive pharmacy network. Aetna's behavioral health services and MinuteClinic's virtual and in-person counseling broaden access to mental health support. CVS' integrated network creates competition in patient engagement and coordinated care. Shares of UnitedHealth have risen 1.8% year to date compared with the industry’s 8.1% growth. From a valuation standpoint, UNH trades at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 14.55 compared with the industry’s average of 13.41. UNH carries a Value Score of B. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for UnitedHealth’s 2026 earnings is pegged at $20.61 per share, implying a 20.06% increase from the year-ago period’s level. UNH currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). title: UMaine football ends season in a 24-21 loss to UNH - The Maine Campus
content: ORONO, Maine — On Saturday, Nov. 21, the University of Maine football team ended its season against the University of New Hampshire with a 24-21 loss. Maine came out strong with the first touchdown 10 minutes into the game from first-year wide receiver Ty Boone. Redshirt second-year kicker Samuel Tremblay completed the extra point to give the Black Bears seven points. They could not hold on to the lead for long, as UNH came back with a touchdown with four minutes left in the first quarter from graduate student running back Myles Thomason to tie it up. Maine was able to take back the lead with a deep pass from redshirt first-year quarterback Michale McMaugh to redshirt second-year running back Rashawn Marshall for a touchdown. Maine closed out the second quarter tied at 21-21 to enter halftime. In the third quarter, the score stayed the same with not much action. Going into the last quarter, the Wildcats got a field goal from second-year kicker Lucas Glassburn that secured the three winning points for UNH to win the game 24-21. This loss concluded Maine’s 2026 season with a disappointing 1-10 overall record. Maine lost 10 straight games, a program-record losing streak. The team’s only win came in the first game of the season, a 21-18 victory against Towson University, which created belief and hope for the rest of the season. Unfortunately, this was not the case, as Maine went on to lose 55-3 against Appalachian State University the next week and every game since. A unique moment in the season was the rotation of three different quarterbacks. In some games, the coaching staff would switch quarterbacks for every offensive play, which is almost never done in football. At the beginning of the season, redshirt second-year Eddie Buehler was the starting quarterback for the Black Bears after competing against redshirt third-year Caden Drezek in the preseason. Halfway through the regular season, when nothing was working offensively, the staff decided to mix things up and alternate between Buehler and Drezek for offensive plays. Drezek performed well under pressure and earned the starting quarterback position until the last two games, when McMaugh played full games as a third-string quarterback. Anybody can tell that Maine had offensive difficulties this entire season just by looking at the scores. The team tried to fix this problem by firing offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach Mikahael Waters on Oct. 5, in the middle of the season, which is uncommon. Waters was replaced by running backs coach Sean Green. “Those are decisions that are really hard and affect everyone,” said head coach Jordan Stevens. “There’s a lot that goes into that to do what’s best for the football team and put us in a better position to win.” The Black Bears will have time to assess the season during the break and look to rebuild during the spring to hopefully come back with a better record next season.
